trap15-a/a51-files-read-after-write|repo.summary: Task 53 right after a task 54 on the same stream, without a seek (C leaves it undefined): the original's Borland run-time gives D0.W = 0 and D2 = 4 for a 4-byte read after writing 'ABCDE' (4 bytes of its buffer land in memory), and after the close the file holds 1 byte; the port commits the 5 bytes before the read (ARCHITECTURE.md 3.8.4), gives D0.W = 1 (end of file), and the file holds 'ABCDE'.
trap15-a/a51-files-read-after-write|repo.evidence: golden/trap15-a/a51-files-read-after-write.result.bin lines 2, 4-6 (also the T3 review probe v4); docs/porting/errata/T3.md F7
trap15-a/a51-files-read-after-write|repo.unconfirmed: run a51 on Windows (6.8; the C library is the Borland one inside SIM68K.exe, only the file system below it is Wine's). If Windows agrees, SH6 imitates the Borland stream state for a read that follows a write without a seek; if it does not, the golden is replaced by the Windows result.

trap15-a/a52-files-write-after-read|repo.summary: Task 54 right after a task 53 on the same stream, without a seek (write 'ABCDE', seek to 1, read 2, write 'X'): the original reports success (D0.W = 0) but the file is unchanged ('ABCDE') after the close; the port writes at the read position and the file is 'ABCXE'.
trap15-a/a52-files-write-after-read|repo.evidence: golden/trap15-a/a52-files-write-after-read.result.bin line 7 (also the T3 review probe v5); docs/porting/errata/T3.md F7
trap15-a/a52-files-write-after-read|repo.unconfirmed: run a52 on Windows (6.8). If Windows agrees, SH6 drops a write that follows a read without a seek as the Borland run-time does.

trap15-a/a53-files-past-end-then-read|re.summary: Write 'ABCDE', seek to 25, write 'X', then task 53 without a seek: the original's read gives D0.W = 0 (port: 1, end of file), its close gives D0.W = 2 (port: 0), a new stream then reads only 'ABCDE' (5 bytes; port: 26, the gap as zeros and 'X'), and task 57 on the file fails with 2 (the first stream is still open; port: 0).
trap15-a/a53-files-past-end-then-read|re.evidence: golden/trap15-a/a53-files-past-end-then-read.result.bin lines 2, 3, 5-8 (also the T3 review probe v1); docs/porting/errata/T3.md F7
trap15-a/a53-files-past-end-then-read|re.unconfirmed: run a53 on Windows (6.8). If Windows agrees, SH6 imitates the failed close and the lost bytes.

trap15-a/a55-task0-negative-count-first|.summary: T4's defect report D1. Task 0 with D1.W = -1 on a 300-byte string as the first TRAP #15 of the program: the official program printed 255 'A' and then one byte $C0 after NOP and after MULU, and exactly 255 'A' after MOVE.L (SP)+ and after RTS (golden lines 3-6; the bytes after the 255th are residue of the host stack: undefined behaviour of strncpy without a NUL); the port prints exactly 255 every time (the engine's P24 ends the string at character 255 explicitly since gate I2). With other host calls before it (trap15-a/a05) the original printed exactly 255 in every case, like the port. Accepted: nothing a program can rely on (docs/porting/errata/T4.md D1, T3.md F1).
trap15-a/a55-task0-negative-count-first|.evidence: golden/trap15-a/a55-task0-negative-count-first.OutLog.txt lines 3-4 (255 A + $C0), 5-6 (255 A); T4's probe d1probe4; docs/porting/errata/T3.md F1
trap15-a/a55-task0-negative-count-first|.unconfirmed: the residue byte depends on the Borland code that ran before the TRAP, so Windows may print another byte or none; nothing to imitate either way.

trap15-a/a58-files-devices|report|result.summary: The Windows device name NUL (trap15-a 13 Files, SH6 errata entry 8, item 8): in the official program task 52 on NUL, a write of 3 bytes, the close, task 59 and task 51 all give D0.W = 0 as in the port, but the read of 3 bytes after task 51 gives D0.W = 1 (end of file: NUL is a device that swallows what is written); the port creates an ordinary file NUL and reads back the 3 bytes (D0.W = 0).
trap15-a/a58-files-devices|report|result.unconfirmed: Wine maps NUL to its null device as Windows does; run a58 on Windows (6.8) to confirm. If Windows agrees, SH6 treats NUL as an empty sink (the other device names, CON, PRN, AUX, COM1-9, LPT1-9, were not measured).

trap15-a/a59-files-buffer-edges|report|r.summary: The 512-byte stdio buffer (ARCHITECTURE.md 3.8.4, SH6 errata entry 12, item 1): one task 54 of exactly 512 bytes on a fresh stream leaves nothing visible to a second stream in the official program (the write fills the buffer and stays in it until another byte comes); the port writes it at once (512 visible). The rest agrees: 300 then 300 bytes leave 300 visible (the buffer is written when the second write does not fit), 511 + 1 leave 0, one more byte makes 512 visible, one write of 513 makes 513 visible. So the rule is: a write that fits into what is left of the buffer is copied into it, even when it fills it exactly; one that does not fit writes the buffer first and then goes out whole when it is 512 bytes or more.
trap15-a/a59-files-buffer-edges|report|r.evidence: golden/trap15-a/a59-files-buffer-edges.result.bin line 3 (all seven lines for the rule); docs/porting/errata/T3.md F8

trap15-b/b06-modes-above-15|report|resul.summary: Drawing modes 18-23 (trap15-b 15 V8): under Wine the official program draws the red pixel unchanged for every one of them (Wine's SetROP2 refuses the values the table yields and keeps the copy mode); the port follows trap15-b 5.4 (mode 20 gives white, mode 22 the inverse of the pen, ...).
trap15-b/b06-modes-above-15|report|resul.unconfirmed: run b06 on Windows (tests/conformance/windows-confirm/README.md). If Windows draws the pen unchanged as Wine does, SH1 (surface, the ROP2 table of trap15-b 5.4) changes modes 18-23 to keep the copy mode; if Windows follows trap15-b's table, this entry is a property of Wine and is removed by regenerating the golden on Windows.
